transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer support. My name is Maya. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Maya. I just bought an Asus RT-AX88U router to replace the standard S-Net hub, but when I plug it into the Openreach ONT, the WAN light stays red and it won't connect to the internet.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your Asus router WAN light stays red when connected to the ONT. Okay. Before we look at settings, Jordon, may I verify your account with your billing address and security question?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, it's 14 Elmwood Drive, Solihull, B91 3TL. And the security question answer is my father's middle name, Edward.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Jordon. That verifies your account. Just to confirm, you are on our Full Fibre 300 package with an Openreach optical ONT.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's right. I'm trying to get my gaming router set up because I need custom port forwarding and VPN client support, but I've been stuck on the Asus setup wizard for two hours and I'm getting really annoyed.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Spending two hours stuck on a setup wizard when you just want to get your gaming setup working is really frustrating, Jordon. I can certainly help you configure those manual WAN settings right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Maya, that's great. I was worried you'd just tell me you don't support third-party routers.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While we cannot troubleshoot the internal Asus firmware features, S-Net fully supports customer-owned routers on our network, and I'll give you the exact WAN authentication parameters you need.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Awesome. I have the Asus web admin interface open on my laptop at 192.168.50.1.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: First, let's verify the physical cabling. Is the blue Ethernet cable connected between Port 1 on the Openreach ONT box and the blue WAN port on the back of your Asus router?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I plugged the Cat6 cable into Port 1 on the optical ONT and into the blue WAN socket on the Asus.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And on the Openreach optical box on the wall, is the LAN 1 indicator illuminated green, confirming an active physical link to the router?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the LAN 1 light on the ONT is solid green, so the physical wire connection is definitely good.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. Now in the left-hand navigation menu of the Asus interface, click on Advanced Settings, and then select WAN.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, clicking Advanced Settings... and WAN. I'm on the Internet Connection tab.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: At the top, what is the WAN Connection Type currently set to?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It says Automatic IP (DHCP).

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is the first reason the WAN light is red. S-Net Full Fibre circuits require PPPoE authentication rather than Automatic IP. Please change that dropdown to PPPoE.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Changing dropdown to PPPoE... okay, now it's asking for a User Name and Password.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: For the User Name, enter your broadband account identifier: broadband@snet-fibre.co.uk. And for the Password, enter: speed300connect.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Entering broadband@snet-fibre.co.uk... and password speed300connect.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And on that same page, make sure the MTU size is configured to 1492, which is the standard packet ceiling for PPPoE encapsulation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Checking MTU... yes, it defaults to 1492.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Next, this is the most critical setting that many users miss: the VLAN tagging. On the left menu under Advanced Settings, click on LAN.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicking LAN now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now look along the top tabs and click on IPTV.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Found it, clicking the IPTV tab.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously third-party routers default to untagged traffic, Jordon, but Openreach optical circuits require a VLAN tag of 101 on the internet port.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ah, okay! Where do I put that in?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under Select ISP Profile, choose Manual Setting. Then in the Internet VID field, enter the number 101. Leave the PRIO field at 0.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Selected Manual... VID entered as 101, PRIO is 0. Do I touch LAN port 1 or 2 VID?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, leave those blank. Now scroll to the bottom of the page and click the Apply button.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicking Apply... it says Applying Settings, please wait while router reboots services.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While we're on the line, did you also want to verify whether IPv6 is enabled on your Asus router?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, does S-Net support native IPv6 on full fiber?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes we do! We provide a native dual-stack /56 IPv6 prefix delegation across all full fiber packages.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's great for multiplayer gaming latency. Where would I enable that in the Asus interface?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In the left menu under Advanced Settings, click on IPv6, set Connection Type to Native, and set DHCP-PD to Enable.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Setting Connection Type to Native... DHCP-PD Enabled... and clicking Apply.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Once applied, the ONT will assign a public 2a02 prefix to your local network devices.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It applied! My laptop just acquired an IPv6 address ending in 41a. That's fantastic.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent, that will give you direct end-to-end routing with no NAT translation required on supported game servers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is exactly what I wanted from this router upgrade.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did you also want to configure custom DNS servers, like Cloudflare or Google DNS?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes! I usually prefer Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 for fastest lookups.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In WAN settings under DNS Server, you can enter 1.1.1.1 and secondary 1.0.0.1 directly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Adding those DNS addresses now and hitting apply.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did you also want to check the Adaptive QoS settings for prioritizing gaming network traffic over background downloads?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, where is Adaptive QoS located in the Asus menu?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In the left menu under General, select Adaptive QoS, toggle the switch to On, and set the priority mode to Games.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Toggling Adaptive QoS on... priority set to Games. That will stop file downloads choking my ping.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Take a look at the front LED on the Asus router. Has the globe icon or WAN light changed color?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes! The WAN light turned solid bright white, no more red!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And on the Asus Network Map, does it show an external WAN IP address assigned under Internet Status?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it says Connected, and there's a public IP address starting with 82.132. The connection status says Your network is online.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Brilliant. Let's open a new tab on your laptop and browse to a couple of websites to make sure DNS and data transmission are operating seamlessly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening YouTube... loaded immediately in 4K. Opening Steam... Steam connected and my game downloads are running at full speed!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's fantastic. You have full Gigabit throughput running through your new Asus gaming router with PPPoE and VLAN 101 fully established.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Maya, you are an absolute legend. I thought I was going to have to return this expensive router. Thank you so much!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are very welcome, Jordon. Just make sure to keep a note of those PPPoE credentials in case you ever factory reset the Asus device.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've written them down in my router manual right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else with your broadband setup I can assist you with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that's everything solved. Have a wonderful day Maya!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Jordon. Enjoy your gaming and have a great afternoon!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks! Bye-bye.
